title: an Action input projecting a field the durable descriptor does have still compiles and runs on both backends
notes: The paired positive control for the three Action-input and timer-duration projection refusals beside it, and it is first-class rather than filler: the rule those cases pin is a NARROWING one -- it newly refuses programs that both implementations used to compile -- and this repository has shipped eleven over-corrections, so a refusal-only set would pin only half of what the change promised. specification/durable-execution.mdx:63, 'Property access and argument passing on a symbolic result MUST create typed projections and dependency edges when representable in Plan IR', is the half this case holds: an index an array descriptor CAN answer is representable, so it must still lower, and the Flow must still emit its descriptor and run. WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY: it is the refusal case with the projection swapped and nothing else changed -- `input.items[0]` where the refusal writes `input.items.length`, over `readonly number[]` into `{ key: number }` so that both spellings type as `number` and the assignability of the Action input is identical either way. A control that differed in its types as well would leave open the possibility that it compiles for some other reason. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING in both of the ways that matter. First, the declared observation: mutating the single stdout line from `static-plan-artifact` to `static-plan-artifact-2` is red on both backends with the stdout diff printed, so the case is not passing on an empty or unread program. Second, and this is the one that says the control sits ON the rule rather than beside it: mutating the SOURCE, `{ key: input.items[0] }` to `{ key: input.items.length }`, turns this program into the refusal on both backends -- SMITHERS4110 at 12:29, `Action ...#Step input cannot project length from durable array`, byte-identical between them. One projection is the whole difference between accept and refuse, measured, on both implementations. The mutator refuses to run unless the case is green on both backends first AND its search string occurs exactly once in the file (it caught the first attempt at the source mutation, where `input.items[0]` also appears in the comment above the code), and every file was restored and sha256-compared byte-identical afterwards.
